A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ConfSMoE research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and relocated or renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original F1/AUC results on four datasets, component and router ablations, computational costs, and embedding and expert-selection analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and reports revised ablation and complexity results, plus new post-imputation attention visualizations.

M1.justification: The confidence router and two-stage imputation design remain. However, v2 explicitly specifies modality-wise attention summation and LayerNorm beyond v1's compact residual update, and rewrites Eq. 5 although both versions describe cross-entropy training. The PDFs do not resolve whether these differences represent procedural changes or fuller and corrected documentation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV, CMU-MOSI, and CMU-MOSEI under the same clinical/sentiment tasks and three missing-modality scenarios. v2's corrected dataset-table entries for MIMIC-IV modalities and 25-PHE classes match descriptions already present in v1; they do not establish expanded coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark and complexity comparisons retain the same baseline methods, including the same dataset-specific participation of SMIL and FuseMoE variants. The router comparison also retains Mean, Softmax, Softmax with load balancing, Gaussian, and Laplacian alternatives.

E3.justification: The complexity comparison is substantively redesigned around controlled model sizes: v1 Table 5 spans roughly 0.10–243.54 million parameters, whereas v2 Table 4 places most models near 2.1–2.4 million, with FuseMoE still larger. Table 3 also changes its stated CMU-MOSI setting from III to II; this is a reported protocol revision, without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a 'w/o post-impute' ablation to isolate the refinement stage and Figures 13–15 to examine attention across modalities and experts. It also revises the existing complexity analysis. These extend retained component and mechanism investigations; the missingness robustness tests and original expert-selection visualizations remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-fold cross-validation with different seeds, list seeds 2023–2025, and use the same plus/minus reporting practice. Changed uncertainty values do not establish a new estimation procedure, additional runs, or new significance testing.

E6.justification: The complexity results are extensively replaced under different model configurations, and several component-ablation outcomes change: MIMIC-III 'w/o impute' F1 changes from 43.79 to 49.59. For the retained CMU-MOSI 50% random-dropout benchmark, token-level F1 changes from 43.89±0.51 to 44.34±0.77 and AUC from 71.51±0.53 to 70.41±1.31. New post-imputation and attention results are added, while the clinical benchmark, CMU-MOSEI, and asymmetric-dropout tables otherwise retain their results.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the main-text softmax Jacobian entry and dimensions, explicitly incorporates Top-K selection into its expression, and extends the gradient-conflict argument to all K, including Top-1. It also revises Eq. 5 and newly asserts its convexity. These are localized mathematical revisions; Appendix B's underlying derivations and entropy assumption remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: confidence-guided routing mitigates expert collapse without load-balancing losses, and two-stage imputation improves missing-modality robustness. The added abstract reference to expert opinions clarifies an existing mechanism rather than introducing another contribution.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the earlier discussion of counterintuitive module-removal behavior with an explanation of ConfNet–imputation complementarity, and interprets the new attention maps as expert-specific refinement. Appendix D replaces the supervision and modality-pool RAM limitations with expert discontinuity and its computational tradeoff against continuous MoE.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the one-layer linear ConfNet and details shared query/key/value projections, attention masking, tensor dimensions, and normalization. It also corrects the dataset summary and clarifies RAM units. Core hyperparameter values, hardware, preprocessing references, and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: The same 41 cited works and substantive related-work positioning are retained. Expanded author names and additional citation placements for already discussed methods do not introduce new research relationships.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the routing and imputation explanations and the ablation and complexity narratives. Dataset and baseline descriptions move to Appendix C, the ablation subsections are reordered, terminology and notation are revised, and the NeurIPS checklist is removed. This materially reorganizes the exposition.

P2.justification: v2 adds three attention-map figures, expands the notation and module-ablation tables, and moves the CMU-MOSI random-dropout table into the appendix. Captions and table labels are updated. The original Figures 1–12 retain their graphical content and the overall visual format remains similar.

improvement.justification: The additional implementation detail, isolated post-imputation ablation, and more closely parameter-matched complexity comparison improve reproducibility and assessment. However, v2 adds an unjustified convexity assertion after Eq. 5, removes the supervision/RAM limitations, and reports CMU-MOSI AUC as 70.41±1.13 in Table 3 versus 70.41±1.31 in Table 9 under the same stated setting. These gains and reliability problems leave the net quality change unclear.
